# APPENDIX `r new_appendix()`. SPATIAL OVERLAY ADDITIONAL INFORMATION {#app:spatial-overlay-additional-information}

```{r}

hbll_sites <- readRDS(here::here("data-generated", "overlays", "hbll-site-summary-table.rds"))

hbll_sites |> 
  select(`Site ID`, `Common Site Name`, `Total transects`, `First survey`, `Last survey`, `No. years`, `E-CP species count`) |>
  flextable() |>
  colformat_int(j = c("First survey", "Last survey"), big.mark = "") |>
  set_table_properties(layout = "autofit") |>
  set_caption("The MPAN Hard Bottom Longline Survey sites in decreasing order of the number of fishing events recorded within site boundaries (2003–2024), showing total transects, first and last survey years, number of survey years, and E-CP species richness. ")

```

# APPENDIX `r new_appendix()`. POWER ANALYSIS SUPPORTING INFORMATION {#app:power}

(ref:conditioning-coefs-caption) Coefficient estimates from the conditioning models. Mean estimates are shown with dots and line segments indicate 95% confidence intervals. Missing coefficients indicate either that the model was not fit because of a lack of encounters (Canary Rockfish and Silvergray Rockfish for HBLL INS N) or because the spatiotemporal random field had collapsed to zero and was omitted from the final model. We do not show uncertainty on the interannual correlation and standard deviation (SD)---they were estimated from the independent year coefficient estimates outside of the sdmTMB model.

```{r conditioning-coefs, fig.cap='(ref:conditioning-coefs-caption)', fig.asp=get_asp(here::here("figures/conditioning-coefs.png")), out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/conditioning-coefs.png"))
```

(ref:sim-posterior-yelloweye-caption) Example simulation replicates illustrating the distribution of real observed historical values (blue) and simulated observations in future years (orange). This shows whether there are obvious systematic differences between the fitted real data and the data simulated from the conditioning model.

```{r sim-posterior-yelloweye, fig.cap='(ref:sim-posterior-yelloweye-caption)', fig.asp=get_asp(here::here("figures/sim-posterior-yelloweye rockfish-HBLL OUT N.png")), out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/sim-posterior-yelloweye rockfish-HBLL OUT N.png"))
```

(ref:sim-posterior-lingcod-caption) Same as Figure \@ref(fig:sim-posterior-yelloweye) but for Lingcod.

```{r sim-posterior-lingcod, fig.cap='(ref:sim-posterior-lingcod-caption)', fig.asp=get_asp(here::here("figures/sim-posterior-lingcod-HBLL OUT N.png")), out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/sim-posterior-lingcod-HBLL OUT N.png"))
```

(ref:sim-posterior-quillback-caption) Same as Figure \@ref(fig:sim-posterior-yelloweye) but for Quillback Rockfish.

```{r sim-posterior-quillback, fig.cap='(ref:sim-posterior-quillback-caption)', fig.asp=get_asp(here::here("figures/sim-posterior-quillback rockfish-HBLL OUT N.png")), out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/sim-posterior-quillback rockfish-HBLL OUT N.png"))
```

(ref:turing-map-quillback-caption) Example real and simulated observations for Quillback Rockfish and the HBLL OUT N survey. The first panel shows the real observations. The other five panels show example replicate simulations. If the conditioning model can represent the spatial patterning of the fitted data, then it should not be obvious which panel contains the real observations.

```{r turing-map-quillback, fig.cap='(ref:turing-map-quillback-caption)', fig.asp=get_asp(here::here("figures/turing-map-quillback rockfish-HBLL-OUT-N.png")), out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/turing-map-quillback rockfish-HBLL-OUT-N.png"))
```

(ref:turing-map-yelloweye-caption) Same as Figure \@ref(fig:turing-map-quillback) but for Yelloweye Rockfish.

```{r turing-map-yelloweye, fig.cap='(ref:turing-map-yelloweye-caption)', fig.asp=get_asp(here::here("figures/turing-map-yelloweye rockfish-HBLL-OUT-N.png")), out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/turing-map-yelloweye rockfish-HBLL-OUT-N.png"))
```

(ref:turing-map-lingcod-caption) Same as Figure \@ref(fig:turing-map-quillback) but for Lingcod.

```{r turing-map-lingcod, fig.cap='(ref:turing-map-lingcod-caption)', fig.asp=get_asp(here::here("figures/turing-map-lingcod-HBLL-OUT-N.png")), out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/turing-map-lingcod-HBLL-OUT-N.png"))
```

(ref:bias-check-caption) Example check of whether the estimation model is able to recover the true simulated recovery rate inside the MPA network without bias. The estimates appear centered on the true value and become increasingly accurate over time. This illustration is just for the 25% increase over 25 years scenario.

```{r bias-check, fig.cap='(ref:bias-check-caption)', fig.asp=get_asp(here::here("figures/bias-check-on-estimate.png")), out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/bias-check-on-estimate.png"))
```

(ref:cumulative-power-caption) Cumulative calculation of statistical power. This is to determine whether sufficient simulation replicates have been run for stable results. For each additional replicate, power is calculated with all replicates up to that replicate and the results become increasingly stable.

```{r cumulative-power, fig.cap='(ref:cumulative-power-caption)', fig.asp=get_asp(here::here("figures/cumulative-power-plot-all-species.png")), out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/cumulative-power-plot-all-species.png"))
```

```{r type-s-error, fig.cap='Type S (sign) error rates by recovery rate, evaluation year, and species. The type S error rate refers to the percentage of significant trends that were in the wrong direction (declines estimated in the MPAN when the truth is an increase). At low levels of power (e.g., in early evaluation years and for small increases), sign errors rates can be substantial, meaning we would could estimate a significant decline just due to noise and chance.', fig.asp=get_asp(here::here("figures/type-s-error-plot.png")), out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/type-s-error-plot.png"))
```

(ref:power-phi-correlation-caption) Correlation plots of correctly signed power against observation error precision from the beta-binomial distribution. Higher precision leads to lower variance. Pearson's correlation coefficients are shown in the top left corner of each panel. Columns show the evaluation year and rows show the percent increase for the inside-MPA sites relative to the outside MPA sites over 25 years.

```{r power-phi-correlation, fig.cap='(ref:power-phi-correlation-caption)', fig.asp=get_asp(here::here("figures/power-phi-correlation.png")), out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/power-phi-correlation.png"))
```

(ref:power-encounter-rate-correlation-caption) Same as Figure \@ref(fig:power-phi-correlation) but with mean encounter rate within the MPA network on the x-axis.

```{r power-encounter-rate-correlation, fig.cap='(ref:power-encounter-rate-correlation-caption)', fig.asp=get_asp(here::here("figures/power-encounter-rate-correlation.png")), out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/power-encounter-rate-correlation.png"))
```

(ref:power-sigma-e-correlation-caption) Same as Figure \@ref(fig:power-phi-correlation) but with spatiotemporal random field standard deviation on the x-axis.

```{r power-sigma-e-correlation, fig.cap='(ref:power-sigma-e-correlation-caption)', fig.asp=get_asp(here::here("figures/power-sigmaE-correlation.png")), out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/power-sigmaE-correlation.png"))
```

(ref:power-sigma-v-correlation-caption) Same as Figure \@ref(fig:power-phi-correlation) but with the standard deviation of the interannual mean (year coefficients) on the x-axis.

```{r power-sigma-v-correlation, fig.cap='(ref:power-sigma-v-correlation-caption)', fig.asp=get_asp(here::here("figures/power-sigmaV-correlation.png")), out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/power-sigmaV-correlation.png"))
```
